meta.title: Flue2Chem — CO₂ capture to surfactant
meta.subtitle: Turning a flue gas stream into a surfactant that today comes from fossil feedstock.
meta.functionalUnit: 1 kg F2C surfactant (Flue2Chem) at the factory gate
meta.boundary: Cradle-to-gate. Starts at the flue gas leaving the stack, ends at surfactant ready to ship. Excludes use phase and end of life.
meta.source: Reproduces standalone/flue2chem-lca-tea.html (Flue2Chem TEA and LCA worksheet) number for number, including its quirks.

notes.title: Flue gas H₂O fraction is never used
notes.text: The dashboard asks for the water mass fraction of the flue gas (0.13) but no formula reads it. Change it and nothing moves. It is kept here as an input so the form matches, and so that you can see that an input with no arrows out of it is a dead parameter.

notes.title: Exhaust is reported net of electrolytic hydrogen
notes.text: The hydrogen made by electrolysis is not a feed that crosses the plant boundary in the worksheet: it is made from water inside the gas-treatment block and subtracted from the exhaust + water stream (exhaust = remaining flue gas + FT flue gas + ethanol wastewater − total H₂). That is why the closure checks flue gas in against products + exhaust out, with no hydrogen term, and why the "mass balance check" row equals the flue gas exactly.

notes.title: Only the Electricity column of the LCIA is live
notes.text: The 18-category ReCiPe results were computed once, offline, per kg surfactant. In the dashboard only the Electricity column responds to your inputs: it is the frozen electricity impact multiplied by (net electricity per tonne of all four saleable products) ÷ 50,312.5 kWh/t, the basis it was originally computed on. Emissions, Infrastructure, Wastewater and the fossil counterfactual never move. Two consequences: at the default inputs the scale factor is 0.19, so the live electricity impact is a fifth of the static figure in the worksheet; and the divisor counts co-product mass although the impact is presented per kg surfactant.

notes.title: An undocumented 0.77 factor is folded into base costs
notes.text: Every equipment base cost except gas treatment is multiplied by 0.77 before the six-tenths rule (e.g. 25.3 × 0.77 = 19.481 m£ for FT synthesis). The worksheet does not say what it is; it is almost certainly a US$ → £ conversion. The same 0.77 also appears inside the FT product upgrading size basis. Both are exposed here as named constants so the assumption is visible.

notes.title: Construction phasing only affects the chart
notes.text: The cash-flow table spreads the total capital over years −2, −1 and 0 (year −3 is zero) and then adds the economic margin discounted to year 0 for 20 years. Nothing in the schedule is time-valued: the capital is neither escalated nor discounted, so the year-20 cumulative is simply −TCI + Σ margin/(1+r)ᵗ. The phasing shapes the cumulative curve but not the NPV.

notes.title: The mass balance runs backwards from the product
notes.text: Surfactant output is fixed first as yield × CO₂ fraction × flue gas. Ethylene oxide, ethanol, its hydrogen and its CO₂ follow from stoichiometric ratios, and whatever recovered CO₂ is left over goes to the Fischer–Tropsch branch. If capture cannot supply what the ethanol route needs (low recovery, high yield) the FT streams go negative and the six-tenths rule returns no cost; the dashboard shows dashes in that case, and so does this model.

stages.title: Mass balance
stages.tryIt: Click the flue gas stream and halve it to 18,000 t/d, then run the mass balance again. Every stream halves and the closure error stays at zero — the balance is linear in throughput. Now click the CO₂ Capture block and drop the recovery to 0.60: the surfactant output does not move, because yield is defined on the raw flue gas, but the CO₂ sent to the FT unit falls sharply.

stages.title: Life cycle inventory
stages.tryIt: Raise the electrolysis demand from 39.4 to 55 kWh/kg H₂ — a realistic commercial figure rather than a near-thermodynamic one — and re-run. Watch how much of the whole inventory is just hydrogen.

stages.title: Impact assessment
stages.tryIt: Cut the electrolysis demand to 20 kWh/kg H₂ and the capture duty to 0.2 GJ/t, as if both ran on far less power, and re-run. Only the Electricity column moves — the other three columns and the fossil benchmark are frozen — and global warming still falls by a sixth: this process is only as clean as the electricity behind it.

stages.title: Capital cost
stages.tryIt: Change the Lang factor from 5.03 to 3.0 and re-run. Total capital drops by 40% without a single piece of equipment changing — which is why the Lang factor is the assumption a reviewer will challenge first.

stages.title: Operating cost & revenue
stages.tryIt: Set the co-product price to zero and re-run. If a process only works when you can sell everything it makes, that is worth knowing before it is built.

stages.title: Profitability
stages.tryIt: Push the discount rate from 10% to 20% and re-run. Compare the minimum selling price against the 7,500 £/t that the fossil-derived surfactant sells for.

scope.tryIt: Before touching anything, note the functional unit. Every number you are about to calculate is “per 1 kg of surfactant” — change the product and none of them are comparable any more.

interpret.tryIt: Go back and change one input at a time by 10%, re-running to the end each time. Electricity cost, Lang factor and surfactant yield will move the answer far more than the rest. Those are the three numbers worth arguing about.

c.label: Carbon
c.source: Used to turn the fossil surfactant's 0.64 kg C/kg end-of-life carbon into CO₂.

flue_in.label: Flue gas throughput
flue_in.source: Stack flow for a large industrial CO2 point source (Flue2Chem basis case).

co2_frac.label: Flue gas CO₂ composition, mass fraction
co2_frac.source: Mass fraction. Post-combustion flue gas is typically 4-15%; 22% reflects an enriched source.

h2o_frac.label: Flue gas H₂O composition, mass fraction
h2o_frac.source: Declared in the worksheet; no formula reads it.

co2_rec.label: CO₂ recovered by capture
co2_rec.source: Capture rate of the absorber. 85-95% is the usual amine-scrubbing design range.

co2_conc.label: CO₂ concentration (w/w) after capture
co2_conc.source: Mass fraction CO2 in the captured gas leaving the capture unit.

h2_co2_ratio.label: H₂ to CO₂ molar ratio
h2_co2_ratio.source: Stoichiometric requirement of the synthesis step; 3:1 is the RWGS/FT design ratio.

surf_yield.label: Surfactant yield
surf_yield.source: kg surfactant per kg CO2 in the raw flue gas - the overall carbon-to-product yield.

opdays.label: Operating days per year
opdays.source: On-stream time. 330 d/y is a common turnaround allowance; 365 assumes continuous operation.

h2_per_eth.label: H₂ per kg ethanol
h2_per_eth.source: Worksheet: H2 to ethanol plant = 0.947 × ethanol.

eo_loss_frac.label: EO carried in the ethanol-rich stream
eo_loss_frac.source: Worksheet: 5% of the EO mass rides along with the ethanol-rich stream and leaves as EO-plant by-product.

eth_coprod_split.label: Ethanol-plant residue to coproduct
eth_coprod_split.source: Worksheet: 44.5% of the ethanol-plant residue is coproduct, the rest wastewater.

elec_cc.label: Electricity required by carbon capture
elec_cc.source: Per tonne of CO2 in the flue gas. Amine capture is typically 0.5-1.2 GJ/t as electricity.

elec_h2.label: Electricity to generate electrolytic H₂
elec_h2.source: kWh per kg H2. 39.4 is near the thermodynamic limit for PEM; commercial units run 50-55.

onsite.label: Onsite electricity generated
onsite.source: Share of consumption met on site rather than imported from the grid.

lcia_base_elec.label: LCIA electricity basis
lcia_base_elec.source: Worksheet: 161 × 1000 / 3.2 MWh per kt of product. Net electricity per tonne of saleable product on which the frozen Electricity column was computed.

fx_base.label: Base-cost conversion factor
fx_base.source: Undocumented multiplier applied to every base cost except gas treatment; presumably US$ → £.

cepci_now.label: CEPCI, current
cepci_now.source: Cost index the equipment costs are escalated to.

ft_feed_lhv.label: Energy content of FT feed
ft_feed_lhv.source: Worksheet: FT synthesis is sized on (CO2-rich gas + H2) × 23 GJ/t expressed as MWe.

ft_upg_co2_yield.label: FT liquids per kg CO₂ in flue gas
ft_upg_co2_yield.source: Worksheet: FT product upgrading is sized on surfactant + 0.16 × CO2 in flue × 0.77.

ft_upg_factor.label: FT upgrading size factor
ft_upg_factor.source: Undocumented 0.77 inside the FT upgrading size basis (same value as the base-cost conversion).

ferm_per_surf.label: Alcohol train throughput per kg surfactant
ferm_per_surf.source: Worksheet: alcohol synthesis, fermentation and EtOH purification are sized on 0.56 × surfactant.

lang.label: Lang factor
lang.source: Total capital divided by delivered equipment cost. 4.7-5.0 for fluid-processing plants (Peters & Timmerhaus).

sprice.label: Surfactant price
sprice.source: Market price of the fossil-derived surfactant this product displaces.

cprice.label: Co-product price
cprice.source: Blended price for FT, ethanol-plant and EO-plant co-products.

flgp.label: Flue gas price
flgp.source: Paid to the emitter for the flue gas. Zero if taken as a free waste stream.

acc.label: Annual capital charge
acc.source: Fraction of total capital charged to each operating year.

indopex.label: Indirect opex / annual delivered equip. cost
indopex.source: Maintenance, insurance and overheads as a fraction of annualised equipment cost.

laboh.label: Labour overhead
laboh.source: Multiplier on base salary covering employment on-costs and supervision.

jobs.label: Number of jobs
jobs.source: Staffing intensity per ktpa of surfactant.

misc.label: Miscellaneous opex / total opex
misc.source: Contingency applied to the sum of variable and fixed operating costs.

irr.label: Internal rate of return
irr.source: Rate used to discount future cash flows. 8-12% is typical for process industry projects.

constr_years.label: Construction years
constr_years.source: Worksheet spends the capital in equal thirds over years −2, −1 and 0.

impacts.label: ReCiPe 2016 midpoint results per kg surfactant (frozen)

components.co2: h2_eth / (h2_co2_ratio * mw.h2 / (h2_co2_ratio * mw.h2 + mw.co2)) * mw.co2 / (h2_co2_ratio * mw.h2 + mw.co2)

gas_ft_ktpa.label: CO₂ rich gas to FT + Alcohol (annual)

gas_ft_co2_ktpa.label: CO₂ in CO₂ rich gas to FT (annual)

gas_eth_ktpa.label: CO₂ rich gas to Ethanol plant (annual)

gas_eth_co2_ktpa.label: CO₂ in CO₂ rich gas to Ethanol (annual)

elec_per_product.label: Net electricity per kg of saleable product

unit_sizes.label: Current sizes, in equipment row order
unit_sizes.expr: concat(size_ft_syn, size_ft_upg, size_alc_syn, size_ferm, size_etoh_pur, size_gas_treat, size_co2_capture, size_surf_synth, size_eo_plant)

equip_cost_row.label: Cost (m£)
equip_cost_row.expr: six_tenths(row.base_gbp, row.size, row.base_size, row.n, row.cepci_base, cepci_now)

cash_ann.label: Ann. DCF (m£)
cash_ann.expr: if(row.year > 0, margin / (1 + irr) ^ row.year, if(row.year > -constr_years, -tci / constr_years, 0))

positive_feed.message: Flue gas throughput must be positive.

ft_branch.message: Recovered CO₂ does not cover what the ethanol route needs; the FT branch has gone negative and its equipment cannot be costed.

lca.basis: Net electricity is divided by the mass of all four saleable products (surfactant and three co-products) before the frozen per-kg-surfactant impacts are scaled.

tea.basis: Co-products are credited as revenue at one blended price; the minimum selling price charges every cost to the surfactant net of that credit.

tornado_mssp.label: What moves the minimum selling price?

price_power_grid.label: NPV against price and power cost
